newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pac BBA sells down PT Dynaplast stake.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pac BBA sells down PT Dynaplast stake.

text.p: Diversified Australian manufacturer Pacific BBA Ltd said on Friday that it had sold part of its minority investment in PT Dynaplast, an Indonesian plastics manufacturer. "A detailed strategic review concluded that the existing investment structure was inappropriate and funds released could be better utilised in the many other growth opportunities within the group," managing director Barry Jackson said in a statement. "At this stage we have sold approximately two thirds of our holding and will sell the balance later in 1997," Jackson said.

"However we will take up an abnormal loss of A$5.9 million in our 1996 financial results to cover the loss on the shares sold to date and the expected loss on the remainder of the holding," Jackson said.
"The release of cash from this investment will be earnings per share positive and Pacific BBA will look for other investment opportunities in Indonesia for each of our divisions," he said.
Dynaplast and Pacific BBA have an excellent relationship and will seek joint investment opportunities," he said.
"PT Dynaplast is achieving strong growth in areas not closely aligned with our core activities and increasing amounts of capital are required to fund this growth," Jackson said.

"While PT Dynaplast is a fine company, our inability to consolidate its results, the lack of liquidity on the Indonesian stock exchange and the ongoing impact of exchange rates have contributed to our decision," he said.
He did not state Pacific BBA's old and new stake in Dynaplast.
Pacific BBA shares closed six cents down at A$4.28.
